name: RA-DT (Retrieval-Augmented Decision Transformer)
venue: ICLR 2025 (arXiv preprint Oct 2024, arXiv:2410.07071; OpenReview submission #9530 to ICLR 2025, primary area: reinforcement learning)
authors_affiliation: Thomas Schmied, Fabian Paischer, Vihang Patil (ELLIS Unit Linz / LIT AI Lab, Institute for Machine Learning, JKU Linz, Austria); Markus Hofmarcher (Extensity AI); Razvan Pascanu (Google DeepMind / Mila / UCL); Sepp Hochreiter (JKU Linz / NXAI). Lead author Thomas Schmied (JKU Linz).
code_url: https://github.com/ml-jku/RA-DT (MIT License; primary language Python; maintainer thomasschmied)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/ml-jku/RA-DT (also releases datasets for Dark-Room, Dark Key-Door, MazeRunner, and Procgen)
task_domain: Decision-making / offline reinforcement learning (in-context RL). Evaluated on grid-world navigation, robotics control, and procedurally-generated video games. Not QA/tool-use/web; it is a sequence-modeling RL agent (Decision Transformer) with external memory.
problem_setting: Offline pre-training of a Decision Transformer on multi-task pre-collected trajectory datasets, followed by interactive test-time evaluation of in-context learning (ICL): after training, the frozen agent interacts with held-out tasks/environments for a fixed number of episodes (ICL trials) without weight updates, and is expected to improve across trials by storing/retrieving its own past experiences. Single-agent, supervision is next-action prediction (cross-entropy for discrete actions, MSE for continuous). No expert demonstrations are required (data comes from PPO behavioural policies); the goal is to enable ICL in long-episode, sparse-reward environments where prior in-context RL methods (which keep entire episodes in context) fail.
what_is_retrieved: Sub-trajectories (fixed-length segments of past experience: sequences of state/action/reward/return-to-go tokens). Values stored in the index are sub-trajectories spanning t-C:t+C (the query segment plus its continuation).
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID. At training time the index is a STATIC store built offline from the pre-collected multi-task dataset D (index = D). At inference/test time the index starts EMPTY and GROWS episodically: the agent writes each completed episode of its own interaction into the retrieval buffer and retrieves only same-task experiences from this growing episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking via maximum inner product search (top-l then reweight to top-k). Not a completeness/minimal-set objective. k is small and fixed (k=1 retrieved sub-trajectory for grid-worlds/Procgen; top-4 concatenated for Meta-World/DMControl). It is a fixed-k similarity-driven selection, not a precision-driven variable-size set.
retrieval_unit: Sub-trajectory: a fixed-length segment of context length C of (state, action, reward, return-to-go) tuples (a (state,reward,action)-tuple sequence rather than a single transition). Keys embed the segment t-C:t; values store t-C:t+C (segment + continuation).
index_source: Hybrid construction. Training: offline-induced static store equal to the pre-collected training dataset D (key-value pairs of all sub-trajectories). Inference: online/test-time-induced store, initialized empty and populated by the agent's own collected episodes during ICL trials.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (Faiss). Authors note HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) graphs are supported for O(log M) search, but for their small RL datasets they use a flat GPU index. So effectively a flat dense vector index; metadata (task ID, episode return) is attached per entry for reweighting.
retriever_type: Dense, training-free / off-the-shelf. Maximum inner product search (cosine similarity) over embeddings produced by an embedding model g. Two variants: (1) domain-specific embedding = a DT pre-trained on the same domain; (2) domain-agnostic = a frozen pre-trained LM (BERT-base-uncased) accessed via the FrozenHopfield mechanism. No learned retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / training-free). The retrieval component requires no training: it uses a frozen embedding model (either a separately pre-trained DT or a frozen BERT via FrozenHopfield) plus cosine-similarity MIPS. Retrieved items are re-ranked by hand-designed relevance + utility heuristics (task-ID match during training, episode return during inference), not a learned signal. Authors note end-to-end training of the retriever (a la Atlas/Izacard) is future work.
query_construction: The current input sub-trajectory tau_in (the agent's recent context of length C) is embedded by g to form query q = g(tau_in). Tokens are aggregated by mean over the context length, using state tokens only (found most effective). Query dropout (drop ~20% of embedded tokens) is applied during training for diversity; query-blending (interpolate query with a random index key, alpha_blend=0.5) is used for Meta-World/DMControl.
query_granularity: Step/state-level (sliding window). During inference the query is reconstructed from the current rolling context window every t environment steps (t=1 for Dark-Room/Key-Door; t=25 for MazeRunner/Meta-World/DMControl/Procgen). During training, queries are formed per sub-trajectory in the batch. Effectively trajectory-segment-level, re-issued repeatedly within an episode.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / fixed schedule. Retrieval is performed repeatedly during environment interaction at a fixed interval of every t steps (t=1 or t=25 depending on environment), not one-shot. There is no uncertainty/learned trigger.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieve every t environment steps (t=1 for Dark-Room and Dark Key-Door; t=25 for all other environments). t trades off inference time vs final performance. No confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger.
reranking: Yes. A two-stage reweighting/reranking: first retrieve top-l (l=50) by cosine similarity, then re-score by s_ret = s_rel + alpha * s_u (relevance = normalized cosine similarity; utility = task-ID match indicator during training, total episode return during inference; alpha=1, scores normalized to [0,1]), then keep top-k. This is a heuristic, metadata-aware reranking (not a cross-encoder).
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank + filtering/regularization. Retrieval regularization is applied during training: deduplication (discard entries with cosine similarity > 0.98; found the most important regularizer), similarity cut-off (discard too-similar neighbours), and query dropout. For grid-worlds, retrieved experiences are replaced with same-task random samples if the query is from very early in the episode (< timestep 10). No LLM distillation/compression of retrieved content.
how_retrieved_used: Latent-token injection via cross-attention into the policy network. Retrieved sub-trajectories are encoded by separate per-token-type embedding layers (state/action/reward/RTG) and fused into the Decision Transformer through cross-attention (CA) layers interleaved after every self-attention (SA) layer; the DT then predicts the next action conditioned on both its input trajectory and the retrieved set. It is not prompt-text augmentation and not skill reuse; it is internal-representation conditioning. Retrieval is used both during training and inference.
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved conditioning within an acting loop (no explicit planner/tree search). RA-DT is a reactive sequence-model policy: at each (or every t) timestep it retrieves relevant sub-trajectories and cross-attends to them to predict the next action. There is no MCTS, plan-then-retrieve, or hierarchical subtask decomposition; retrieval is woven into the per-step action-prediction rollout.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step (per environment-step / per action-prediction). Retrieval+conditioning happens at each action-prediction step (or every t=25 steps for harder envs) within an episode rollout; there is no CoT/per-sentence reasoning since this is a non-language RL policy.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw sub-trajectory (the actual stored state/action/reward/RTG token sequence, including its continuation t-C:t+C), embedded and injected as latent/soft representations via cross-attention. Not a distilled strategy, free-text workflow, or executable program.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw trajectory segment (low abstraction). Retrieved units are concrete past sub-trajectories, not distilled strategies, guidelines, skills, or workflows.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware training plus retrieval regularization. Training with retrieval (rather than random sampling) teaches the model to use bursty, relevant context; deduplication (cosine > 0.98 removed), similarity cut-off, and query dropout prevent the model from copying near-identical retrieved trajectories (delusions/copying behaviour). Reweighting by task-ID (train) / return (inference) steers retrieval toward useful, high-reward, same-task experiences. No learned relevance evaluator / self-reflection.
memory_type: episodic (external vector-index memory of sub-trajectories). It is an episodic / experience replay-like external memory, conceptually a non-parametric complementary-learning-systems component alongside the parametric DT.
write_back: True. At inference, the agent writes each completed episode of its own environment interaction into the (initially empty) retrieval buffer/index, enabling later retrieval of its own past experiences. At training, the index is pre-built from the offline dataset (no online writes during training beyond initial construction).
online_growth: Yes (at test/deployment time). The inference-time vector index starts empty and grows as the agent stores each completed ICL-trial episode; subsequent retrievals draw from this accumulating same-task memory. The training-time index is frozen after offline construction.
write_back_trigger: On episode completion (per-trial), unconditional. After each ICL trial/episode during inference, the whole episode trajectory is appended to the index (Algorithm 1, line 13: I <- I union tau). Writes are not gated on success/failure or self-critique; deduplication can optionally avoid storing redundant experiences. During training, writes happen once at index-construction time.
failure_experience_usage: Stores all experiences regardless of outcome (both successful and unsuccessful episodes are written to the index), but does NOT use failures contrastively or as corrective rules. Instead, return-based reweighting at inference up-weights high-return (successful) sub-trajectories so the agent is steered toward high-reward behaviour; low-return experiences are de-prioritized rather than exploited as negative signal. Authors note next-action-prediction cannot distinguish positive/negative examples (a limitation).
memory_evolution_update: Append-only with deduplication. New episodes are appended to the index; entries are not mutated, merged, or refined after writing. Deduplication (similarity > 0.98) prunes/avoids redundant entries, but stored sub-trajectories themselves are immutable.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is a fixed similarity top-l MIPS followed by heuristic reweighting (relevance + task/return utility) and top-k selection; it is not an RL- or learning-optimized retrieval policy. The authors explicitly leave end-to-end retriever training as future work.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Single-agent private memory in the experiments, but the design explicitly supports cross-agent sharing: the external memory can hold experiences from other agents (training data comes from multiple PPO agents), and the authors note the memory enables leveraging 'experiences from other agents' and distant-past experiences (e.g., continual learning). No heterogeneous multi-framework sharing is demonstrated.
benchmarks: Dark-Room (10x10, 20x20, 40x20 grids); Dark Key-Door (10x10, 20x20, 40x20); MazeRunner (15x15 procedurally-generated mazes); Meta-World (ML45 train / ML5 hold-out); DMControl (DMC11 train / DMC5 hold-out); Procgen (16 games; PG12 train / PG4 hold-out; settings PG12-Seen, PG12-Unseen, PG4).
benchmark_family: decision-RL / in-context RL. Grid-world navigation (Dark-Room, Dark Key-Door, MazeRunner), embodied/robotics continuous control (Meta-World, DMControl), and procedurally-generated video games (Procgen). Not D4RL; these are standard in-context-RL and multi-task RL benchmarks.
baselines: Vanilla Decision Transformer (DT, Chen et al. 2021); Algorithm Distillation (AD, Laskin et al. 2022); Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT, Lee et al. 2023). RA-DT itself is reported in two variants: domain-specific embedding (DT encoder) and domain-agnostic embedding (FrozenHopfield + BERT). Internal ablation baselines include random sampling (uniform / same-task) instead of retrieval.
key_metrics: Primary metric: mean episode reward / return on held-out tasks at the end of the ICL trials (with 95% confidence intervals over 3 seeds), tracked as ICL performance improvement across trials (40 trials Dark-Room/Key-Door, 30 trials MazeRunner). Also reported: data-normalized scores (Meta-World/DMControl/Procgen), context-length usage, and training/inference efficiency (samples/sec, speedup).
headline_result: On grid-worlds (Dark-Room, Dark Key-Door, MazeRunner) RA-DT outperforms AD, DPT, and vanilla DT in final ICL reward while using only a fraction of their context length (RA-DT uses ~50-transition context vs ~2-episode / up to ~2000-step context for baselines). On Dark-Room 10x10 RA-DT reaches near-optimal reward with both domain-specific and domain-agnostic (BERT) embeddings; it is the only method to improve across the 30 ICL trials on MazeRunner. On the largest grid (40x20) RA-DT is ~7x faster to train than baselines. On complex environments (Meta-World, DMControl, Procgen) RA-DT improves average hold-out performance but no method (including RA-DT) exhibits genuine in-context improvement (a reported negative result/limitation).
ablations: All ablations on Dark-Room 10x10. (E.1) Retrieval vs sampling: training with retrieval beats both uniform and same-task random sampling (retrieval builds 'bursty' sequences important for ICL; uniform sampling yields poor ICL). (E.2) Reweighting: task-based reweighting during training is critical; no reweighting (alpha=0) drops performance sharply; sensitivity analysis shows robustness across a range of alpha. (E.3) Retrieval regularization: deduplication (sim > 0.98) is the most important regularizer; similarity cut-off and query dropout also help, preventing copying behaviour. (E.4) Query construction: mean aggregation over state tokens only is best vs actions/rewards/RTG/all/last-hidden. (E.5) Cross-attention placement. (E.6) Steps between retrievals (t) trades inference cost vs performance. (E.7) Training efficiency: ~7x faster on 40x20 due to shorter context. (E.8) Inference efficiency: slightly slower when retrieving every step, comparable when retrieving less frequently; FlashAttention important for long context. (E.9) Domain-agnostic LM choice: BERT best vs smaller LMs. (E.10) Effect of k on AD. (E.11) Convergence of baselines.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end RL task metrics (episode reward/return, ICL improvement) are reported; intrinsic retrieval-quality metrics (Recall@k, nDCG, retrieval precision) are not reported separately. Some qualitative retrieval/attention-map analysis is provided (Appendix D.1.1) but not quantified as a decoupled retrieval metric.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final/cumulative episode reward and ICL improvement across trials). Some process-level analysis is qualitative: attention-map analysis showing the agent attends to the retrieved sub-trajectory, and exploration analysis (delusion/copying behaviour), but no quantitative step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: RA-DT uses a much shorter context (50 transitions) vs ~2 episodes (up to ~2000 steps) for AD/DPT/DT, giving ~7x faster training on Dark-Room 40x20 (samples/sec). Retrieval adds embedding+search overhead: at inference RA-DT is slightly slower than baselines when retrieving every step (t=1) but comparable when retrieving every t=25 steps. Faiss flat/HNSW index gives O(log M) scalable search; deduplication reduces index size and speeds retrieval. FlashAttention is highlighted for handling long context efficiently.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed, small context budget. DT context length C=50 transitions (100 for 20x20/40x20 Dark variants). Retrieval: top-l=50 retrieved then reweighted to top-k; top-k after reweighting = 1 for grid-worlds/MazeRunner/Procgen, top-k = 4 (concatenated, ordered by return) for Meta-World/DMControl. Fixed-k, not adaptive/budget-capped.
builds_on: Decision Transformer (Chen et al. 2021) as the policy backbone; Retrieval-augmented generation in LLMs, especially RETRO (Borgeaud et al. 2022) for the value=segment+continuation design and cross-attention fusion, and kNN-LM / RAG (Khandelwal 2019; Lewis 2020); FrozenHopfield mechanism (Paischer et al. 2022) for the domain-agnostic LM-based trajectory encoder; BERT (Devlin et al. 2019); Faiss (Johnson et al. 2019; Douze et al. 2024) for the vector index; multi-task DT datasets/embedding-space observations from Schmied et al. 2024; reweighting by relevance+utility following Park et al. 2023.
contrasts_with: Prior in-context RL methods that keep entire episodes in context: Algorithm Distillation (AD, Laskin et al. 2022) and Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT, Lee et al. 2023), and vanilla DT. RA-DT contrasts by retrieving only relevant sub-trajectories into a short context window. Also contrasts with RAG methods relying on expert demonstrations (Humphreys et al. 2022 RAG-Go) and domain-specific embedding models, since RA-DT needs neither expert demos nor a domain-specific encoder. Distinct from online in-context RL (AdA/Team et al. 2023) and in-context imitation learning (Raparthy et al. 2023).
lineage: Group F (decision/memory RL): retrieval-augmented / external-memory in-context reinforcement learning. Sits in the lineage of episodic-memory RL and RETRO-style retrieval augmentation applied to Decision-Transformer-based in-context RL; a bridge between offline sequence-modeling RL agents and growing-memory experience retrieval, distinct from classic static-corpus RAG planners.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as CBR). If mapped loosely: Retrieve = yes (MIPS over sub-trajectory memory); Reuse = yes (cross-attention conditioning on retrieved segment); Revise = no explicit case adaptation/revision; Retain = yes (append episodes to memory at inference). Flags: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: no, Retain: yes].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) / episodic external memory for in-context RL.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/skills/documents are indexed; retrieved units are RL sub-trajectories).
index_content_separation: Partial. Keys are lightweight embeddings (g(tau_{t-C:t})) while values store the heavier raw sub-trajectory with continuation (tau_{t-C:t+C}); this separates retrievable index keys from loaded content, but not a progressive-disclosure / SOP-index-then-content tool pattern.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index or integration protocol such as RapidAPI/REST/MCP; the index is a Faiss vector store of trajectory segments, static at training and grown at inference).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tools or inter-tool dependencies are modeled).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A for CBR-style adaptation. The retrieved sub-trajectory is used verbatim (as raw segment) and conditioned on via cross-attention; there is no LLM-prompted or execution-feedback case revision. Closest analog: latent conditioning rather than explicit adaptation.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (this is a primary method/empirical paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: Authors release new datasets for four environments (Dark-Room, Dark Key-Door, MazeRunner, Procgen). Construction: PPO behavioural agents generate offline data (Dark-Room/Key-Door: 100K transitions per goal for 10x10/20x20, 200K for 40x20; 80 train / 20 eval goals; MazeRunner: 100K interactions per maze over 100 train mazes, 20 eval; Meta-World ML45=90M transitions, ML5 hold-out; DMControl DMC11=11M transitions, DMC5 hold-out; Procgen PG12=24M transitions (2M/task) from task-specific PPO agents trained 25M steps on 200 seeds, PG4 hold-out). Verifiability is via environment reward (programmatic).
